Urmila dropped by on a Sunday and found Rafiq at the desk with a whiteboard schedule behind him.
"When did you start doing this?" she asked.
"The second week after the layoff," Rafiq said. "I stayed in bed till noon three days running, and I felt awful. So I asked myself what changed. It was that the days had no shape. If I give them one, my head stays out of the hole."
"So what's the shape?"
"A walk at seven. Four hours at the desk, applications first, then a course. And one call a day to a real person, not about work."
"Only four hours?"
"Four good ones. Then I stop. Today's call is you."
Urmila laughed. "Then I'm glad I came."

qa.q: What time is the morning walk?
How did Rafiq feel during the days spent in bed till noon?
qa.a: Rafiq felt awful, and he linked it to days that had no shape.

qa.q: What could Rafiq change if the four desk hours stop bringing progress?
qa.a: Rafiq could keep the structure but swap what the four hours are used for, such as adding a mock interview or a small project.

qa.q: How might Urmila have felt on seeing the whiteboard schedule?
qa.a: Urmila was probably relieved and impressed to see Rafiq organised, and pleased to be that day's call.

grounding: The dialogue shows a person who, knowing unstructured days bring low mood, sets a walk, a block of desk work and a daily call.

passage:
The first week after the layoff, I had no structure at all. I woke at ten, scrolled job sites in bed, ate lunch at four, and by evening felt heavy and useless. On Friday I noticed it: the days with nothing fixed were the days I felt worst.
So I built a frame on the back of an envelope. 7 am: a walk round the lake, no phone. 9 to 1: applications and one hour of study, at the dining table, dressed as if for work. Afternoons: free. And one call a day with a real person. Shalini, my college friend, volunteered for Mondays and Thursdays.
It isn't magic. Some days the four hours feel like forty. But on the walk I sometimes think of a better line for a cover letter, and after talking to Shalini I remember I'm more than my job title.
— Preeti

qa.q: What time was the lake walk?
How did Preeti feel on the days with nothing fixed?
qa.a: Preeti felt heavy and useless on those unstructured days.

qa.q: What else could Preeti add if the four hours start feeling too long?
qa.a: Short breaks between applications and study, or a mid-morning check-in with Shalini, to keep momentum without burning out.

qa.q: What might Shalini get from the Monday and Thursday calls?
qa.a: Shalini gets to support a friend in a concrete way and is likely reassured to hear how Preeti is doing.

grounding: It shows someone after a layoff reasoning that unstructured days bring low mood and fixing a morning walk, four hours of work and a daily call to keep going.

passage:
Career counsellor's note, 22 April.
Hemant came in two weeks after being laid off from the design agency. He said his days had "no edges": sleeping late, applying in bursts at midnight, not seeing anyone. He had noticed himself that his mood was lowest on the days with no plan.
We did not start with jobs. He sketched a daily frame himself: a 7 am walk to the tea stall and back, applications and portfolio work from 9 to 1, lunch with his mother, and one call or meeting with a person each afternoon. He said, "If I leave it loose, I'll drift."
We agreed he would try it for two weeks and tell me honestly which parts didn't work. He also has our helpline number in case the low days get heavier. Next session: 6 May.
— Jomon

qa.a: 7 am, to the tea stall and back.

qa.q: What does Hemant's phrase "no edges" suggest he was feeling?
qa.a: He felt adrift and low, with nothing to hold his days together.

qa.q: What else did the counsellor put in place?
qa.a: A two-week trial with honest feedback, a next session on 6 May, and the helpline number in case the low days get heavier.

qa.q: How might Hemant's mother experience the daily lunch?
qa.a: She gets regular time with him and can see how he's doing, which may ease her worry.

grounding: It shows a young man after a layoff noticing that shapeless days lower his mood and setting a daily walk, work block and social contact to keep going.
